classification.difficultyReason: Identify the two given sides and their included angle, substitute directly into the cosine rule and take the positive square root. Obtuse angles use the same taught procedure.

content.prompt: In each triangle, calculate the unknown side length, giving your answer correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: Triangle with 7 cm left side, 9 cm lower side and their included angle marked 64 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Unknown side opposite the included angle of 64 degrees.

answer.worked:
Let the unknown side be $x$ cm. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=7^2+9^2-2\times7\times9\cos64^\circ\\x&=\sqrt{7^2+9^2-2\times7\times9\cos64^\circ}\\x&\approx8.65\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with 8 cm upper side, 10 cm lower sloping side and their included angle marked 21 degrees at the right vertex.

answer.worked:
Let the unknown side be $x$ cm. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=8^2+10^2-2\times8\times10\cos21^\circ\\x&=\sqrt{8^2+10^2-2\times8\times10\cos21^\circ}\\x&\approx3.82\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with 10 cm side from upper left to lower middle, 8 cm horizontal lower side and included angle 130 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Unknown side opposite the obtuse included angle.

answer.worked:
Let the unknown side be $x$ cm. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=10^2+8^2-2\times10\times8\cos130^\circ\\x&=\sqrt{10^2+8^2-2\times10\times8\cos130^\circ}\\x&\approx16.34\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with two given sides each 4 cm meeting at a lower-middle vertex with included angle 120 degrees.

answer.worked:
Let the unknown side be $x$ cm. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=4^2+4^2-2\times4\times4\cos120^\circ\\x^2&=48\\x&=4\sqrt3\\x&\approx6.93\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
